entities.summary: Eileen Chang (traditional Chinese: 張愛玲; simplified Chinese: 张爱玲; pinyin: Zhāng Àilíng; Wade–Giles: Chang1 Ai4-ling2；September 30, 1920 – September 8, 1995), also known as Chang Ai-ling or Zhang Ailing, or by her sometime pen name Liang Jing (梁京), was a Chinese and American writer. Chang was born in Shanghai to a family with aristocratic lineage and received a bilingual education in Chinese and English. She gained literary prominence in Japanese-occupied Shanghai between 1943 and 1945. In 1952, she left the newly founded People's Republic of China for British Hong Kong and later the United States.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent Chinese-American writer, Eileen Chang's works influenced the development of modern Chinese literature and provided insight into the experiences of Chinese women during World War II. Her writing also helped shape the identity of Chinese diaspora communities in the United States.
